D1.query: Can an employer terminate a probationary employee without prior notice?
D1.proposition: An employer may terminate the services of a probationary employee without giving the employee prior notice.
D1.supports: court says a probationer can be discharged/terminated simpliciter without notice, enquiry or opportunity (non-punitive termination)
D1.opposes: court holds notice/show-cause/enquiry/statutory notice or compensation is required before terminating a probationer (e.g. punitive/stigmatic termination, standing orders, Art. 311, s.25F)
D1.note: Termination of PERMANENT/confirmed employees, gratuity, back wages, resignation are different conditions.

D2.query: Can anticipatory bail be granted to an accused in a serious offence?
D2.proposition: Anticipatory bail under s.438 CrPC may be granted to an accused charged with a serious offence.
D2.supports: court holds/affirms that gravity of the offence does not bar s.438 relief (no offence is excluded) or that it was rightly granted
D2.opposes: court holds relief is not available / must be refused or is restricted for serious offences (economic offences, special statutes, heinous crimes), or sets aside a grant for that reason
D2.note: Regular bail (s.437/439) and bail after arrest are different conditions.

D3.query: Can delay in filing an appeal be condoned by the court?
D3.proposition: A court may condone delay in filing an appeal.
D3.supports: court holds delay can/should be condoned on sufficient cause, or condones it, with reasoning
D3.opposes: court holds delay cannot be condoned (no power / no sufficient cause / statutory outer limit) or refuses condonation with reasoning
D3.note: A bare order 'Delay condoned.' without reasoning is background, not a court position on the legal question.

T1.query: Is a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act maintainable without a statutory demand notice?
T1.proposition: A complaint under s.138 NI Act is maintainable even though no statutory demand notice was given to the drawer.
T1.supports: court holds the complaint can proceed without a demand notice (or that notice is not a pre-condition)
T1.opposes: court holds a statutory demand notice (and the 15-day period) is a mandatory ingredient/condition of the offence
T1.note: Facts merely stating that a notice was sent are background.

T2.query: Can a High Court quash an FIR in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure?
T2.proposition: A High Court may quash an FIR in exercise of its inherent powers under s.482 CrPC.
T2.supports: court affirms the power exists / holds it was (or should have been) exercised to quash an FIR in the case
T2.opposes: court holds the power may not be used to quash in the situation (e.g. serious offence compromise, investigation at nascent stage) or sets aside a quashing order
T2.note: Statements that the power is to be used 'sparingly' while affirming it exists are MIXED only if the court denies quashing for the case at hand; if it only describes the standard, use MIXED with MEDIUM/LOW or NEUTRAL.

T3.query: Can a court set aside an arbitral award under Section 34 on the ground of erroneous interpretation of the contract?
T3.proposition: A court may set aside an arbitral award under s.34 of the Arbitration Act merely because the arbitrator erroneously interpreted the contract.
T3.supports: court holds that an erroneous (or unreasonable) interpretation of the contract is itself a ground for setting aside
T3.opposes: court holds that erroneous interpretation / error of law / re-appreciation is not a ground, the court does not sit in appeal, the arbitrator's possible view must stand
T3.note: Patent illegality and perversity are grounds, but a passage saying only that patent illegality exists is MIXED unless it says whether mere erroneous interpretation suffices.

T4.query: Is a confession made to a police officer admissible in evidence?
T4.proposition: A confession made to a police officer is admissible in evidence against the accused.
T4.supports: court holds such a confession is admissible (e.g. under a special statute such as POTA s.32 / MCOCA s.18)
T4.opposes: court holds it is inadmissible under s.25/26 Evidence Act (general rule) or the equivalent
T4.note: Section 27 discovery (partly admissible) is MIXED unless the proposition is limited to s.27.

T5.query: Is circumstantial evidence sufficient to sustain a conviction?
T5.proposition: A conviction may be sustained on circumstantial evidence alone.
T5.supports: court affirms conviction can rest on circumstantial evidence if it is complete and consistent (the five principles)
T5.opposes: court holds circumstantial evidence was insufficient in the case or cannot alone sustain conviction
T5.note: Statement of the five principles as the test for when conviction is sustainable is SUPPORTS (the proposition is the general rule); outcome acquittals on facts are OPPOSES only if the court says the evidence was insufficient.

T6.query: Is prior sanction required to prosecute a public servant for corruption?
T6.proposition: Prior sanction is required before a public servant can be prosecuted for corruption.
T6.supports: court holds sanction is mandatory/required (s.19 PC Act, s.197 CrPC) for the prosecution
T6.opposes: court holds sanction is not required (retired servant, act not in official duty, offence outside the section, MLAs)
T6.note: Passages about sanction for other offences are different conditions.

T7.query: Is reservation in promotion permissible for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes?
T7.proposition: The State may provide reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
T7.supports: court holds Art. 16(4A) permits it / upholds reservation in promotion
T7.opposes: court holds reservation in promotion is not permissible or is restricted by conditions the proposition lacks (quantifiable data, adequacy, efficiency) and applies them to deny
T7.note: Reservation in appointment, seats, or other categories is a different condition.

T8.query: Can the court enhance compensation for land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act?
T8.proposition: A court may enhance the compensation awarded for land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
T8.supports: court enhances compensation / affirms the power to do so
T8.opposes: court refuses to enhance, sets aside an enhancement, or holds the court cannot enhance in the situation
T8.note: Facts of an award or a claimant's prayer are background.

T9.query: Can a person claim title by adverse possession against the true owner?
T9.proposition: A person can acquire title by adverse possession against the true owner.
T9.supports: court affirms adverse possession can ripen into title (and may be used as sword/shield)
T9.opposes: court holds adverse possession fails / cannot be claimed in the case, or restricts it so the answer is no
T9.note: A passage stating the elements that must be proved is MIXED/NEUTRAL (conditions), not support, unless the court applies them to grant or deny.

T10.query: Is a divorced wife entitled to maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure?
T10.proposition: A divorced wife is entitled to claim maintenance under s.125 CrPC.
T10.supports: court affirms a divorced wife can claim/obtain maintenance under s.125
T10.opposes: court holds a divorced wife cannot (remarried, personal law bar, other Act displaces it)
T10.note: Maintenance for a wife during marriage, children or parents is a different condition.

T11.query: Can a landlord evict a tenant on the ground of bona fide personal requirement?
T11.proposition: A landlord may obtain eviction of a tenant on the ground of the landlord's bona fide personal requirement.
T11.supports: court affirms/grants eviction on bona fide need or affirms the ground exists
T11.opposes: court refuses eviction because need is not bona fide or the ground is unavailable
T11.note: Eviction on other grounds (sub-letting, default) is a different condition.

T12.query: Is an insurance company liable to pay compensation when the driver did not hold a valid licence?
T12.proposition: An insurer is liable to pay compensation (at least in the first instance) even though the driver did not hold a valid driving licence.
T12.supports: court holds the insurer must pay (pay-and-recover) to the third party despite the licence defect
T12.opposes: court holds the insurer is absolved of liability because of the licence defect
T12.note: Insurer liability for other reasons (no premium, no permit) is a different condition.

F1.query: Can bail be granted to an accused in an offence under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act?
F1.proposition: Bail may be granted to an accused charged with an offence under the NDPS Act.
F1.supports: court affirms bail can be granted under s.37 conditions or grants/upholds bail in an NDPS case
F1.opposes: court holds bail cannot be granted (s.37 not satisfied) or sets aside bail for that reason
F1.note: Bail under other statutes (PMLA, UAPA) is a different condition.

F2.query: Is an oral agreement for sale of immovable property enforceable by a suit for specific performance?
F2.proposition: An oral (unwritten/unregistered) agreement for sale of immovable property can be enforced by a suit for specific performance.
F2.supports: court holds an oral agreement can be specifically enforced
F2.opposes: court holds a written/registered agreement is required or the agreement is unenforceable for lack of writing/registration
F2.note: General specific-performance principles for written agreements are different conditions (NEUTRAL).

F3.query: Can an FIR be registered for a cognizable offence without a preliminary inquiry?
F3.proposition: Police may register an FIR for a cognizable offence without first conducting a preliminary inquiry.
F3.supports: court holds registration is mandatory and no preliminary inquiry is permissible when information discloses a cognizable offence
F3.opposes: court holds a preliminary inquiry is permitted/required in the case in question (the listed categories) before registering
F3.note: A passage reciting both the rule and the categories is MIXED.

F4.query: Is an ex parte decree liable to be set aside under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure?
F4.proposition: An ex parte decree can be set aside on application under Order IX Rule 13 CPC.
F4.supports: court affirms the remedy exists / sets aside an ex parte decree under the Rule
F4.opposes: court holds the application is not maintainable or is refused in the case (e.g. after appeal dismissed)
F4.note: Conditions (service of summons, sufficient cause) described neutrally are context or MIXED.

F5.query: Can a dying declaration alone form the basis of conviction?
F5.proposition: A reliable dying declaration, without corroboration, can alone form the basis of a conviction.
F5.supports: court holds a truthful, voluntary dying declaration can be the sole basis of conviction
F5.opposes: court holds a dying declaration cannot alone support conviction (must be corroborated) in the case
F5.note: The proposition already says 'reliable'; statements that the court must be satisfied of reliability support it.

F6.query: Is a daughter entitled to a share in coparcenary property under the Hindu Succession Act?
F6.proposition: A daughter is entitled to a share in coparcenary property under the Hindu Succession Act (as amended in 2005).
F6.supports: court holds a daughter is a coparcener by birth / entitled to a share
F6.opposes: court holds she is not entitled (pre-2005 position applied, tribal exclusion, other bar)
F6.note: Class I heir shares in intestate succession of separate property are a different condition.

F7.query: Can a government employee be dismissed from service without holding a departmental inquiry?
F7.proposition: A government employee may be dismissed from service without a departmental inquiry.
F7.supports: court holds dismissal without inquiry is permissible (Art. 311(2) provisos, probation, rules)
F7.opposes: court holds an inquiry/opportunity is mandatory before dismissal and a dismissal without it is bad
F7.note: Procedure within an inquiry, gratuity, or suspension is a different condition.

F8.query: Can interest be awarded on compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act?
F8.proposition: Interest may be awarded on compensation awarded under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
F8.supports: court awards or affirms power to award interest on MV Act compensation
F8.opposes: court holds interest cannot be awarded or disallows it
F8.note: Quantum of compensation heads (consortium, income) is a different condition.
